gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the battery makers' cycle-life claims on one depth-of-discharge basis. The only ladder I could open is LiTime's, relayed by Nautworthy: 4,000 cycles at 100% DoD, 6,000 at 80% and 15,000 at 60%. If WattCycle's '15000+ Deep Cycles' title uses a basis like LiTime's 60% figure, it is not a bigger number than Redodo's '4000+ Cycles'. I could not open WattCycle's page to confirm its basis.
standout_why: I compared against Nautworthy's LiTime page (r2 result 12, not cited), our own Dealectric page, and the result titles ChatGPT got. Nautworthy already prints LiTime's three-step ladder, so the pages ChatGPT got hold part of the finding. What none of them does is set it beside the WattCycle '15000+' and Redodo '4000+' title claims. I wanted two more normalisations: WattCycle '120A BMS' against a possible 100 A continuous rating, and Vatrer's 150 A as continuous or peak. I couldn't open a maker page for either, so neither is sourced. ChatGPT already noticed the WattCycle 120A/100A conflict in one chat (r1x1).
decides: On its own this doesn't change the pick. It only removes '15000+ cycles' as a reason to prefer WattCycle, and only once WattCycle's basis is confirmed. A finding that could decide the pick is still unsourced: whether WattCycle's 120 A and Vatrer's 150 A are continuous ratings, and whether each surge figure comes with a duration. Two things would do it: WattCycle continuous turning out to be 100 A, or Vatrer's 150 A turning out to be a peak. Either would collapse the 'more headroom' argument behind ChatGPT's Vatrer and WattCycle picks.

findings.label: Cycle life by depth of discharge (maker figures, relayed)
findings.value: 4,000 cycles at 100% DoD; 6,000 at 80% DoD; 15,000 at 60% DoD
findings.source_title: LiTime 12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth Lithium Deep Cycle Battery: Specs, Real-World Figures & Fit | Nautworthy
findings.note: Nautworthy credits these figures to LiTime's product page and says it did not test the battery. No end-of-life capacity threshold (such as 80% or 70% retained) is given. The 15,000 figure is 3.75× the 100% DoD figure only because it is counted at a shallower discharge, so it is not a longer life at full use.
